newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian security operation to flush out rebels.
newsitem.headline: Algerian security operation to flush out rebels.

text.p: Security forces have trapped a group of Moslem rebels in a bomb factory south of Algiers and are trying to drive others from their longtime stronghold in the area, Algerian newspapers said on Tuesday.
La Tribune newspaper said security forces had circled the bomb-making plant near Sidi Moussa in Blida province south of Algiers, a known bastion of armed Islamists.
It said rebels had mined access points to the laboratory "in which are made most of the bombs which spread death in the Algiers area".
It added: "Two to three hundred 'terrorists' are scattered in the nearby mountains watching for the slightest letup in vigilance to commit another crime."
El Watan, one of Algeria's best-informed newspapers on security issues, said security forces were carrying out a major assault on the "nerve centre" of the armed groups.
"Sidi Moussa sheltered, and shelters still, the most important laboratories for bomb-making used during attacks in the Algiers area," it said.
In an article on the region, El Watan said security forces and "Patriots" -- community groups armed by the government -- were slowly trying to recover the area from "terrorist" hands.
Algerian officials and media use the term "terrorist" to mean armed Moslem fundamentalists who have been fighting since early 1992 to try to topple the authorities.
About 60,000 people have been killed in the conflict, many by car bombs and other explosives planted with no warning.
El Watan said Ouled Allel, a village of 8,000 people taking in part of Sidi Moussa, had been abandoned by its inhabitants in 1994 and taken over by "terrorists" and used for production of bombs.
"They have planted explosive devices everywhere, in buildings and roads which lead to their strongholds," it quoted a Patriot as saying.
"The process of making these bombs and material used are the work of an engineer known throughout the region by the name of Kamel TNT..."
El Watan said there was a reward of two million dinars ($36,000) on the "terrorist's" head.
"During the past two days, Algerian army troops have succeeded in de-mining several houses...Explosions have been heard over a range of a dozen kms," the paper said.
It quoted a Patriot as adding: "It is a very difficult job. They know the booby-trapped places and can move in safety. While we, we don't know where to step. Each step we take can be fatal...."
